title: Runtime: add KV/prefix cache event hooks (lookup/insert/evict) + request correlation
creator: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Context
- This is part of the Cache hit-rate instrumentation sprint (telemetry v2). We need runtime-level hooks for KV/prefix cache events that are attributable to the request that triggered them.
- This ticket covers *event hook points + correlation plumbing* only. Per-request outcome classification + saved_prefill_ms/hit-bytes accounting is tracked in ENG-4814.

Goal
Implement lightweight runtime instrumentation for prefix/KV cache events:
- cache.lookup
- cache.insert
- cache.evict

…and correlate events to the active request without exporting high-cardinality request identifiers downstream.

Acceptance criteria
- Correctness
  - Every cache event emitted from the runtime can be associated with a request context internally (at least: request_correlation_id + route/model/version placeholders).
  - Lookup events record whether a candidate entry was found and whether it was usable (e.g., found-but-invalid / found-but-too-short / etc. as a small finite enum).
  - Insert/evict events include stable cache key identifiers (hashed/bucketed) suitable for aggregation and debugging without leaking raw prefixes.
  - No behavior change to cache policy/algorithm.
- Performance
  - Instrumentation overhead <1% at p95 latency on cache-heavy workloads (prefill+decode mixed), measured via perf-canary and local microbench.
  - No additional allocations on the hot path in steady state (avoid per-event heap allocations; pre-allocate buffers or use thread-local counters).
- Operability
  - Behind a runtime feature flag (default off). Flag must be dynamically togglable via existing runtime config reload.
  - Safe failure mode: if telemetry sink is unavailable/backpressured, instrumentation must degrade gracefully (drop events, increment a drop counter).

Non-goals
- Defining the v2 metric schema/tag set (owned by Telemetry; see spec/ADR).
- Computing saved_prefill_ms / hit-bytes (ENG-4814).
- Adding gateway/control-plane fields (ENG-4816).

Implementation notes (proposed)
Hook points
- lookup: inside PrefixCache::Lookup() after key hashing and before returning the cache entry (or miss).
- insert: after successful prefill when we commit a new prefix segment to cache.
- evict: in eviction path (LRU/size pressure), include eviction reason enum.

Correlation strategy
- Introduce an internal RequestContext handle that is set on the worker thread while executing a request.
- Store a small correlation token (u64) derived from the request’s trace/span id (or runtime-generated monotonic id) in TLS.
- Emit events with:
  - request_corr_id (u64) (NOT exported as a tag; included only in structured event payload for sampled debugging)
  - cache_key_hash (u64) derived from normalized prefix bytes + model_id salt
  - event_type enum (lookup/insert/evict)
  - lookup_result enum (hit/miss/invalid/short/etc.)
  - cache_tier enum (prefix_cache vs kv_cache if both paths exist)
  - reason enum for evict (capacity/lru/ttl/manual)

Overhead controls
- Single branch on the hot path: if (!cache_telemetry_enabled) return.
- Aggregate counters in thread-local structs; export periodically (existing stats tick) rather than emitting a structured event per operation, except when sampled.
- Sampling: fixed-rate sampler for structured events (default 0.1% of requests) gated by feature flag; counters always on when enabled.
- Drop behavior: bounded ring buffer for sampled structured events; on overflow drop and increment cache.telemetry.dropped.

Testing plan
- Unit tests
  - Verify correlation token propagation through request execution (including streaming code paths).
  - Verify event enums are within allowed ranges.
  - Verify no PII/raw prefix bytes are serialized.
- Integration tests
  - Synthetic cache hit/miss workload: assert counters increment as expected.
  - Eviction stress test: force evictions and validate reason mapping.
- Performance
  - Local microbench: measure p50/p95 latency and CPU overhead with flag off vs on.
  - Perf-canary: run cache-heavy scenario; ensure p95 delta <1% and no QPS regression.

Open questions
- Do we standardize on trace/span id for request_corr_id (preferred for cross-system debugging) vs runtime monotonic id (simpler)? If trace ids are used, confirm they’re available on all request types (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- For cache_key_hash, confirm the normalization boundary (raw prompt bytes vs normalized prefix tokens). Current plan is to hash a stable representation from the cache key object (post-normalization) to avoid drift.

Links
- Related sprint umbrella: ENG-4812 (project)
- Follow-up: ENG-4814 (outcome classification + saved_prefill_ms/hit-bytes)
- Pipeline/schema: ENG-4815
- Attribution tags: ENG-4816
- Runtime PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18421

Reviewer notes / checklist
- Ensure no new allocations on lookup path (check flamegraph / heap profiles).
- Ensure event emission cannot block request execution (no locks in hot path).
- Ensure correlation context is correctly cleared on request completion to prevent cross-request contamination.
- Ensure feature flag behavior matches rollout plan (default off; can enable per region/tier via control plane).
comments: 2025-02-10 (Samir Qureshi): Implemented first pass of TLS-based RequestContext + hook calls in PrefixCache::{Lookup,Insert,Evict}. Feature flag: runtime.cacheTelemetryV2.enabled (default false). Added drop counter when ring buffer overflows. PR up: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18421. Pending: eviction reason enum mapping review + ensure correlation context is cleared on early-exit/stream cancel.

2025-02-12 (Marcus Reed): Ran microbench on A100 and L4. With flag off: no measurable change. With flag on + counters only: +0.3% p95. With sampled structured events @0.1%: +0.5% p95. Looks within budget. Please double-check there are no allocations in lookup path when sampling is disabled; I saw 1 alloc in a debug build that might be from formatting/logging.

2025-02-14 (Noah Patel): Reviewed PR. Main concern: request_corr_id derived from trace id is fine, but make sure it never becomes a metric tag downstream. Keep it in structured payload only, and ensure payload sampling is per-request (not per-event) so we don’t get skewed sequences. Also verify context is propagated through the streaming retry path (known issue area).

2025-02-18 (Omar El-Sayed): Marking In Review. Please address Noah’s notes (streaming retry + context clearing). Also align naming with spec: use event names that map cleanly to cache.lookup/cache.insert/cache.evict; avoid one-off names that will diverge from dashboards.
